1281:
(a) The City may suspend or revoke the City issued license of any location owner or location operator to manufacture, distribute, or sell alcoholic beverages as a penalty for the conviction of the business owner or business operator of a violation of O.C.G.A. § 16-12-35(e), (f), or (g) or for a violation of one or more provisions of this chapter. Violation of any provision of this chapter may also be punished in accordance with the general penalty section of the City Charter.
(b) The City may suspend or revoke the license of any location owner or location operator of any other license granted by the City as a penalty for the conviction of the business owner or business operator of a violation of the O.C.G.A. § 16-12-35(e), (f), or (g).
(c) The suspension or revocation of licenses under this Code section shall be in accordance with the following guidelines of due process:
(1) No license which has been issued or which may be issued pursuant to this chapter shall be suspended or revoked except for due cause and after hearing and upon prior three-day written notice to the holder of the license of the time, place and purpose of the hearing and a statement of the charges upon which the hearing shall be held, unless such hearing has been waived pursuant to stipulation as provided under Subsection (8). Such notice shall provide the reasons for the suspension or revocation sought and shall be mailed or delivered to the holder of the license.
(2) The term "due cause" for the purposes of this section shall include, but not be limited to:
(A) Conviction of, or the entering of a plea of guilty or nolo contendere by, the licensee or any of his employees or any person holding an interest in the license for any felony, any law, administrative regulation or ordinance involving alcoholic beverages, gambling or narcotics, or tax laws.
(B) Conviction of, or the entering of a plea of guilty or nolo contendere by, the licensee or any of his employees or any person holding an interest in the license for any sex offense when the licensed business is for on-premises consumption.
(C) Suspension or revocation of any state license required as a condition for the possession, sale or distribution of alcoholic beverages.
(D) Material falsification of any fact given in an application for a license issued under this chapter or bearing upon the licensee's qualification therefor. Any act which may be construed as a subterfuge in an effort to circumvent any of the qualifications for a license under this chapter shall be deemed a violation of the requirement attempted to be circumvented.
(E) Failure to meet or maintain any standard prescribed by this chapter as a condition or qualification for holding a license.
(F) Any other factor known to or discovered by the City whereby it is objectively shown the licensee, any of the licensee's employees or any person holding an interest in a license, has engaged in conduct at or involving the licensed business or has permitted conduct on the licensed premises that constitutes a violation of federal or state law, local ordinance or administrative regulations involving alcoholic beverages, gambling or narcotics for all alcohol licensed businesses and including any sex offense under state law or local ordinances with respect to businesses licensed for on-premises consumption. With respect to this section, it shall be rebuttably presumed that the violative act was done with the knowledge or consent of the licensee; provided, however, that such presumption may be rebutted only by evidence which precludes every other reasonable hypothesis save that such licensee did not know, assist or aid in such occurrence, or in the exercise of full diligence that such licensee could not have discovered or prevented such activity.
(3) Notice of suspension or revocation proceedings shall be served on the person named as licensee in the application. Notice shall be in writing. The notice may be served personally or by first class mail. If by mail, the notice shall be addressed to the licensee at its address as provided by the licensee to the municipality. The burden shall be on the licensee to provide notice, in writing, of any change of address for service of notices and process. In the case of service by mail of any notice required by this chapter, the service is complete at the time of deposit in the United States Postal Service.
(4) The hearing shall be conducted by a hearing officer appointed by the Mayor. The hearing officer shall be an attorney licensed to practice in the state who is disinterested in the proceeding.
(5) Hearings shall be only as formal as necessary to preserve order and shall be compatible with the principles of justice. The City Attorney shall present the City's case and bear the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that due cause exists to suspend or revoke the license. At the hearing, the licensee shall have the right to represent itself or be represented by counsel, may cross examine all witnesses offered by the City, and may call witnesses and present evidence in its own behalf. Formal rules of evidence shall not apply to hearings under this section, although the hearing officer shall have the right to exclude evidence which carries no indicia of reliability. All testimony shall be offered under oath or affirmation.
(6) The hearing officer shall make his final determination within ten business days of the completion of the hearing. The decision shall be placed in writing and contain the hearing officer's findings of fact, conclusions of law, and decision as to sanction, if any. Such sanction may include one or more of the following: revocation of the license, suspension of the license for no more than 12 months, imposition of a probationary period not to exceed 12 months, and/or a civil monetary penalty not to exceed the amount allowed under the City's Charter. Progressive sanctions, depending on the severity of the violation, are encouraged but not required. Where the remaining term of the license is less than 12 months, imposition of suspension or probation for a period in excess of the term of the existing license shall be applied to any renewal license. A subsequent violation within a probationary period shall be cause for revocation and/or denial of license renewal. A total of three separate and unrelated violations within 24 months, whether or not within a probationary period, shall be grounds for permanent revocation.
(7) The hearing officer's decision shall be personally served or mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested to the licensee and his attorney, with a copy to the City Attorney, within ten business days of the close of the hearing. The decision of the hearing officer shall constitute final action by the City, subject to review upon petition for certiorari to the County Superior Court.
(8) Upon receipt of notice of adverse action against the licensee under this section, the licensee may waive its right to a hearing and stipulate to a sanction, as recommended by the City Manager, in consultation with the Chief of Police.
Any stipulation entered under this subsection shall be in writing, signed by the licensee, and non-appealable.
(Ord. No. 1346, § 1, 11-15-2023)

1284:
All businesses operating as an amusement game room hereunder shall be subject to the following regulations:
(a) Devices to be kept in plain view; gambling devices prohibited. All bona fide coin operated amusement machines shall at all times be kept and placed in plain view of and open and accessible to any person(s) who may frequent or be in any place of business where such machines are kept or used. Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize, permit or license any gambling device of any nature whatsoever. To satisfy the "plain view" requirements of this section, all bona fide coin operated amusement machines shall be visible through a window from the exterior of the location and shall also be visible from the main entryway of the location. No bona fide coin operated amusement machine shall be located behind a doorway, in a back room, in a side room, or in any other location that is not in "plain view" as defined by this section.
(b) Inspection. The chief of police or his/her designee may inspect or cause the inspection of any location in which any such bona fide coin operated amusement machine(s) are operated or set up for operating, and may inspect, investigate and test such machines as needed.
(c) Attendant required. It shall be unlawful for any location owner or location operator to open the location to the public unless an attendant is present. Said attendant shall be of sufficient mental and physical capacity so as to be able to provide aid to patrons if needed or desired. Said attendant shall not be less than 18 years of age.
(d) Loitering. As used in this section, "loitering" shall mean remaining idle in essentially one location and shall include the concepts of spending time idly, loafing or walking about aimlessly, and shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation licensed to operate an amusement game room to permit loitering on or in the immediate vicinity of any machine or business premises regulated hereunder in such a manner as to:
(1) Create or cause to be created a danger of a breach of the peace;
(2) Create or cause to be created any disturbance of the peace, as defined by law;
(3) Obstruct the free passage of pedestrians or vehicles; or
(4) Obstruct, molest or interfere with any person lawfully in a public place.
(e) Shirt and shoes required. All location owners and location operators shall require shirts and shoes to be worn at all times by any person frequenting their location.
(Ord. No. 1346, § 1, 11-15-2023)

1295:
(a) No license for a massage establishment shall be granted to any person who is not a citizen of the United States or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence.
(b) No person, partner or officer less than 18 years of age shall be granted a license for a massage establishment.
(c) In addition to obtaining an occupation tax certificate as referenced in Section 9-2-1, any person desiring to obtain a massage establishment license or massage therapist license shall make application to the City Manager or his/her designee. All applications shall be sworn to by the applicant as true, correct and complete before a notary public or other officer authorized to administer oaths. All applications shall be in writing and shall set forth the following information:
(i) The full legal name of the applicant, including all aliases, nicknames, pseudonyms or trade names currently or heretofore used by the applicant;
(ii) The current and all previous business and residence addresses of the applicant within the three years immediately preceding the date of application;
(iii) Written proof that the applicant is over the age of 18 years;
(iv) The applicant's height, weight and color of eyes and hair;
(v) Two current photographs of the applicant at least two inches by two inches in size;
(vi) The business, occupation or employment of the applicant for three years immediately preceding the date of application;
(vii) Any massage or similar business license history of the applicant, including whether such person, in any previous operation in any jurisdiction, has had such a license revoked or suspended, the reason therefor, and any business activity or occupation subsequent to the action of suspension or revocation;
(viii) A list of all services to be provided;
(ix) Authorization for the City, its agents and employees to seek information and conduct an investigation into the truth of the statements set forth in the application and the qualifications of the applicant(s) for the license;
(x) All convictions, pleas of guilty, or pleas of nolo contendere for violations of any law and the grounds therefor;
(xi) A complete set of fingerprints of the applicant, the operator(s), the owner(s) and all employees:
A. Authority. This subsection is enacted pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 35-3-35(a)(1.2), the Georgia Umbrella Statute entitled "Dissemination of information to public agencies, political subdivisions, authorities, and instrumentalities."
B. Fingerprinting required. An individual seeking to receive a massage establishment license or a massage therapist license shall be fingerprinted as a condition of submitting an application for said license. By filing such application, the applicant consents to the City obtaining their criminal history record information (CHRI) from the Georgia Crime Information Center (GCIC) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).
C. Access authorized; usage regulations. The City is hereby authorized to access national criminal history record information pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 35-3-35(a)(1.2).
1. Information obtained and handled for any purposes pursuant to this subsection shall comply with all Georgia laws and the Federal Privacy Act.
2. No information given as part of the request for a criminal history and no record obtained pursuant to this section may be entered on any database.
3. No information given or obtained pursuant to this section shall be subject to the provisions of the Georgia Open Records Act.
D. Administration; fees; procedures.
1. Applicant shall provide his/her fingerprints, which may be taken by the City of Conyers Police Department or may be taken by the Rockdale County Sheriffs Office if the City Police Department is unable to do so.
2. The applicant shall bear the cost of: (1) fingerprinting if carried out by the Rockdale County Sheriff; (2) the charge by the GBI and the FBI for the CHRI history at their latest rate, paid to the City by certified or cashier's check or money order; and (3) an administrative fee allowed by statute to be charged by the City, which shall be the maximum allowed by statute, which is currently $20.00, which fee shall include fingerprinting when carried out by the Conyers Police Department.
3. (a) The City Manager's designee shall provide written notice to the applicant or license holder of their order to deny, suspend or revoke the application or license. All decisions by the City Manager shall be in writing and shall be served on the aggrieved person personally or by registered certified mail and mailed to the address set forth in the applicable license or permit application.

Notice of the appeal shall be delivered in writing to the Clerk of the City of Conyers. The Mayor and City Council shall set a hearing date within ten days of receiving the appeal request. Notice of said hearing shall be mailed to the applicant or license holder at the address shown on the applicant's application or the license. The Mayor and City Council may require the submission of additional written evidence from the aggrieved person and shall hold a hearing on the matter. At the hearing, the aggrieved person or his/her representative is entitled to be heard and present evidence on their behalf. The City Manager's designee, the City Manager may similarly be heard and present evidence in support of the denial, suspension or revocation. The Mayor and City Council shall determine whether the denial, suspension or revocation of the permit is justified, utilizing the criteria for denial, suspension or revocation set forth in this chapter.

d. No information given or obtained pursuant to this section shall be subject to the provisions of the Georgia Open Records Act.

a. Applicant shall provide his/her fingerprints, which may be taken by the City of Conyers Police Department or may be taken at any Georgia Applicant Processing Services location so long as the applicant registers in such a manner that allows the Conyers Police Department to receive the criminal history results.
b. The applicant shall bear the cost of the electronic fingerprinting submission services set by the Georgia Applicant Processing Services and an administrative fee allowed by statute to be charged by the City, which shall be the maximum allowed by statute, which is currently $20.00, which fee shall include fingerprinting when carried out by the Conyers Police Department.

If the CPD determines that the spill is a level I spill, the wrecker service shall be responsible for cleaning the scene of the accident, including removing all debris from the street in connection with towing a vehicle. This requirement shall be strictly enforced by the CPD. ii. If the CPD determines that the spill is a level II or level III spill, the Rockdale County Fire Department shall determine what action shall be taken as to the cleanup and disposal of the spill.

(Ord. No. 1242, § 1, 2-17-2021)
1314:
(a) All wrecker services provided services via the wrecker service rotation list shall charge the fees set forth by the Georgia Department of Public Safety for non-consensual towing.
(b) In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 35-1-4, the wrecker service shall not charge storage fees for any reported stolen vehicle until 24 hours after the owner has been notified of recovery of the vehicle.
(c) Any wrecker service that is found charging fees or rates greater than those provided herein shall be removed from the wrecker service rotation list for a period of time to be determined by the Chief of Police.
(d) The fee schedule shall be posted in open view to the public in the wrecker service's lobby. In addition, the wrecker service shall be responsible for delivering, at the wrecker service's expense, to each owner or representative of every towed vehicle present at the scene of the tow, a pre-printed disclosure that states the general fees to be charged by the wrecker service, the types of payment accepted by the wrecker service, the location of the impound lot, the normal business hours for times of vehicle release and the phone number(s) of the wrecker service.
(e) In order for a wrecker service to maintain eligibility to remain on the wrecker service rotation list, the wrecker service shall furnish the person who pays for wrecker services a written receipt that contains an itemization of all charges, and the telephone number and website for CPD personnel to receive comments about the wrecker service.
(f) All charges and fees for towing and storage of the vehicle towed shall be at the expense of the owner of the vehicle and against the vehicle itself as provided by State law. All liability and responsibility for payment for the services of the wrecker service shall lie with the owner/operator; neither the City nor any employee of the City shall be responsible for payment.
(g) The wrecker service shall not charge the City any fee to tow any City owned vehicle or any vehicle that the City impounds or needs towed related to a pending investigation or seizure.
(h) The wrecker service shall not charge the City any fee to store any vehicles that are involved in an investigation by the CPD.
(i) For every vehicle that is towed as a result of a City-initiated call off of the wrecker service rotation list, the wrecker service shall remit $20.00 to the City. These fees shall be remitted to the City on or before the tenth day of the month for the preceding month. The remittance shall include an itemized statement that reflects the time, date, and location of each tow for which payment is being remitted.
(Ord. No. 1242, § 1, 2-17-2021)
1315:
(a) In order for a wrecker service to remain eligible to be on the City's wrecker service rotation list, the wrecker service shall:
i. Comply with all of the obligations set forth in this chapter.
ii. Maintain a daily list of vehicles towed and/or stored for CPD-initiated towing and storage services. The list shall contain details as to the make, year, model, color, VIN, license plate number, name of owner, and the purpose of removing and/or storing the vehicle. The records shall be retained for a period of 12 months and shall be made available to the CPD for review and copying during normal business hours.
iii. Be responsible to the vehicle owner for all damages incurred during towing and storage of any vehicles entrusted to them.
iv. Have a response time of 20 minutes or less for at least 90 percent of all calls per month. Response time is the time elapsed from the time the 911 center contacts the wrecker service until the time that the wrecker actually arrives at the location of the vehicle that is to be towed.
v. Cooperate with all duly authorized law enforcement officers in the protection of any evidence or in any investigation arising out of a wreck or seizure of a vehicle by any such law enforcement officers.
vi. Ensure that their wrecker service operators maintain a valid commercial/driver's license as required by law.
(b) All wrecker services applying for a position on the wrecker service rotation list and all wrecker services wishing to remain on the wrecker service rotation list shall maintain, while on the wrecker service rotation list, in the wrecker service's name at a minimum the following insurance coverage:
i. An automobile liability insurance policy having a single event coverage of not less than $300,000.00;
ii. A comprehensive general liability policy providing bodily injury coverage limits of $100,000.00 per person and $300,000.00 per occurrence and property damage coverage limits of $100,000.00 per person and $300,000.00 per occurrence;
iii. Cargo and garage keepers liability insurance with a limit of $300,000.00; and
iv. Worker's compensation insurance in the minimum coverage required by Georgia law.
(c) Said insurance policies shall name the City of Conyers as an additional insured under the policy and shall provide for written notification within 15 days of policy modification, expiration or cancellation. The wrecker service shall provide to the Chief of Police or his/her designee a full copy of each insurance policy no later than five days from being placed on the wrecker service rotation list or extension thereof or any modification of the insurance policy and upon renewal of the insurance policy.
(Ord. No. 1242, § 1, 2-17-2021)
1316:
(a) In the event that an application for placement on the wrecker service rotation list is denied, then the Chief of Police or his/her designee shall provide written notice to a wrecker service rotation list applicant of the Chief of Police's or his/her designee's decision to deny said wrecker service rotation list application. Such written notification shall set forth in reasonable detail the reasons for such action and shall notify the applicant of the right to appeal under the provisions of this chapter.
(b) An applicant may appeal the denial of a wrecker service rotation list application by providing written notification to the Chief of Police within ten calendar days of the denial of the wrecker service rotation list application. The written notification shall include the legal and factual basis upon which the applicant's appeal is based.
(c) The Chief of Police or his/her designee shall set an administrative hearing date that shall occur within 30 calendar days of the filing of the appeal request. Notice of said administrative hearing shall be mailed to the wrecker service rotation list applicant at the address shown on the wrecker service rotation list applicant's application.
(d) At the administrative hearing, the wrecker service rotation list applicant is entitled to be heard and present evidence on his/her behalf. The Chief of Police or his/her designee shall determine whether the denial of the wrecker service rotation list application is justified using a preponderance of the evidence standard.
(e) The Chief of Police or his/her designee shall consider the following factors in determining whether to uphold the denial of an application:
(i) Compliance with the criminal history requirements;
(ii) Compliance with the requirements of this chapter;
(iii) The history of and facts relating to previous violations of this chapter;
(iv) Compliance with the City's Code of Ordinances, the Georgia Public Service Commission Regulations and State law;
(v) Documented efforts at avoiding violations of this chapter, this Code, PSC Regulations or State law;
(vi) Community involvement; and
(vii) Any other objective and relevant facts.
(f) The Chief of Police or his/her designee, after hearing evidence, shall have the authority to uphold, modify or overturn the Chief of Police or his/her designee's previous decision. The Chief of Police or his/her designee shall issue a written decision on the appeal within 30 calendar days of the date of the administrative hearing. All decisions by the Chief of Police or his/her designee shall be mailed to the wrecker service rotation list applicant at the address set forth in the application.
(g) Any applicant may appeal the Chief of Police's decision to the City Manager within 30 calendar days of the date that the adverse decision is issued by the Chief of Police. Notice of the appeal shall be delivered in writing to the Clerk of the City. The written notification shall include the legal and factual basis upon which the applicant's appeal is based.
(h) The City Manager shall set a hearing date within 30 calendar days of receiving the appeal request. Notice of said hearing shall be mailed to the applicant at the address shown on the applicant's application. At the hearing, the applicant is entitled to be heard and present evidence on his/her behalf. The Chief of Police or his/her representative may similarly be heard and present evidence in support of the denial. The decision of the Chief of Police shall not be set aside unless the City Manager finds it to be:
i. Contrary to law or ordinances; or
ii. Unsupported by substantial evidence on the record as a whole; or
iii. Unreasonable.
(i) All decisions of the City Manager shall be final. The City Manager shall issue a written decision on the appeal within 30 calendar days of the date of the hearing. All decisions by the City Manager shall be in writing and shall be mailed to the applicant at the address set forth in the application.

1317:
Whenever in this chapter any act is prohibited or whenever in this chapter the doing of any act is required, where no specific penalty is provided therefor, the violator of any such provision shall be subject to prosecution in Conyers Municipal Court for a violation of the applicable ordinance and shall be subject to the penalty provisions contained in Section 7-103 of the City Charter and further the violator and the wrecker service shall be subject to the administrative penalties as set forth herein.

The Chief of Police or his/her representative may similarly be heard and present evidence in support of the imposition of the administrative penalty(ies). 1320:
This chapter shall be known, cited and referred to as the City of Conyers Vaping Ordinance.
(Ord. No. 1279, § 1, 2-16-2022)
1321:
(a) The Mayor and City Council do hereby find that certain studies have found a link between e-cigarette or vaping products, which can lead to lung injury, asthma, cardiovascular disease, hospitalization and even death.
(b) Accordingly, the Mayor and City Council find and declare that the purpose of this chapter is to protect the public health and welfare by prohibiting stores that sell vaping products and vape juice from operating in the City.
(Ord. No. 1279, § 1, 2-16-2022)
1322:
The following words and phrases, whenever used in this chapter, shall be construed as defined in this section.
Vape or vape juice refers to any liquid that contains compounds containing pharmaceutical grade vegetable glycerin, propylene glycol, nicotine, food grade flavoring, or water, and can be used for vaping by means of an alternative nicotine product.
Vaping products refers to any products or devices that employ an electronic heating element, power source, electronic circuit, battery, or other electronic, chemical, or mechanical means to produce a vapor that delivers nicotine, synthetics, or illegal substances to the person inhaling from the device, including electronic cigarettes, electronic cigars, electronic hookahs, electronic bongs and electronic pipes, whether manufactured, distributed, marketed, or sold as an electronic cigarette, electronic cigar or electronic pipe. This definition shall not apply to medical treatments prescribed or administered by medical professionals to reduce inflammation in the bronchial airways. This definition shall include vape juice.
Vape shop means any business whose principal product line for retail sale is alternative nicotine products, vape juice or vape products. For the purposes of this chapter, "principal" shall mean that alternative nicotine products, vape juice or vape products constitute at least 25 percent of the business's aggregate retail sales.
(Ord. No. 1279, § 1, 2-16-2022)
1323:
(a) In all zoning districts of the City, vape shops are considered objectionable and are prohibited.
(b) Any vaping shop shall be declared to be nonconforming and shall be regulated as set forth in Section 8-7-96 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 1279, § 1, 2-16-2022)
1325:
This chapter shall be known, cited and referred to as the City of Conyers Hookah Ordinance.
(Ord. No. 1323, § 1, 5-17-2023)
1326:
The following words and phrases shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them herein unless the context clearly indicates a contrary meaning:
Hookah means a single or multi-stemmed water pipe and any associated products and devices which are used to produce fumes, smoke and/or vapor from the burning of material including, but not limited to, tobacco products, shisha or other plant materials.
Hookah bar or lounge means any business in which hookah is used, smoked, burned, inhaled, exhaled, or sold. All hookah bars or lounges shall comply with all of the requirements of the Georgia Smoke-Free Air Act of 2005 and the Conyers Smoke-Free Air Ordinances as set forth in Title 9, Chapter 11 of this Code. A hookah bar or lounge shall be operated as an accessory use to a nightclub or drinking place, as those terms are defined in Title 8, Chapter 7 of this Code and shall not be operated as a stand-alone principal use.
Shisha means a flavored or syrupy mixture of tobacco or herbal products which is intended to be smoked/consumed by a user through a hookah.
(Ord. No. 1323, § 1, 5-17-2023)
1327:
(a) Required. All persons, firms, companies, partnerships, corporations or other such entities desiring to operate a hookah bar or lounge shall, prior to commencing such business, comply with all rules and regulations adopted by the governing authority regulating the operation of hookah bar or lounge. It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to operate a hookah bar or lounge without having first obtained a license therefore. All licenses shall expire on December 31 of the calendar year in which it was granted, and reapplication shall be required for each year thereafter.
(b) Application. The application shall include, but shall not be limited to, the information required on all occupational tax returns, along with the following:
(1) Name, age and residence address of the owner-applicant;
(2) If the owner-applicant is a corporate entity, the names and addresses of the officers or members; the name and address of the registered agent and the registered office of the corporate entity; the state, county, and date of incorporation or formation; and the complete names and addresses of the manager or managers of the proposed hookah bar or lounge;
(3) The name of all shareholders holding 20 or more percent of any class of corporate stock;
(4) The address of the location where the hookah bar or lounge is to be located and operated;
(5) All the previous experience the manager and owner(s) have had in operation of hookah bar or lounges;
(6) Any hookah bar or lounge license history of the owner-applicant and the manager, including whether such person, in any previous operation in any jurisdiction, has had such a license revoked or suspended, the reason therefor, and any business activity or occupation subsequent to the action of suspension or revocation;
(7) The name and address of owner of the property where the hookah bar or lounge is to be located; and
(8) A complete set of fingerprints of the applicant, the manager(s) and the owner(s) (hereinafter collectively referred to as "applicant"):
a. Authority. This subsection is enacted pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 35-3-35(a)(1.2), the Georgia Umbrella Statute entitled Dissemination of Information to Public Agencies, Political Subdivisions, Authorities, and Instrumentalities.
b. Fingerprinting required. An individual seeking to receive a hookah bar or lounge license shall be fingerprinted as a condition of submitting an application for said license. By filing such application, the applicant consents to the City obtaining their criminal history record information (CHRI) from the Georgia Crime Information Center (GCIC) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).
c. Access authorized; usage regulations.
i. The City is hereby authorized to access national criminal history record information pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 35-3-35(a)(1.2).
ii. Information obtained and handled for any purposes pursuant to this subsection shall comply with all State laws and the Federal Privacy Act.
iii. No information given as part of the request for a criminal history and no record obtained pursuant to this section may be entered on any database. No information given or obtained pursuant to this section shall be subject to the provisions of the Georgia Open Records Act.
d. Administration; fees for Conyers Police Department; procedures.
i. Applicant shall provide his/her fingerprints, which may be taken by the City Police Department or may be taken by the Rockdale County Sheriff's Office if the City Police Department is unable to do so.
ii. The applicant shall bear the cost of:
(1) Fingerprinting if carried out by the Rockdale County Sheriff;
(2) The charge by the GBI and the FBI for the CHRI history at their latest rate, paid to the City by certified or cashier's check or money order; and
(3) An administrative fee allowed by statute to be charged by the City, which shall be the maximum allowed by statute, which is currently $20.00, which fee shall include fingerprinting when carried out by the City Police Department.
iii. Upon receipt of the fingerprints and the appropriate fees, the City will transmit said fingerprints and appropriate fees (unless a satisfactory billing arrangement has been entered into between the City Police Department and the GCIC and/or FBI) to the GCIC. As provided by law, the GCIC will compare the subject's fingerprints against its criminal file and submit the fingerprints to the FBI for a comparison with nation-wide records, unless submission to the FBI is automatic pursuant to the use of live-scan. The results of the FBI check will be returned based on its current procedure, presently being directly to the City Police Department if submissions are made manually to the GCIC, or electronically from both the GBI and FBI where submissions are made electronically to the GCIC.
iv. In compliance with Federal Law 95-544, which provides for the rendering of a fitness determination, the City will decide whether the record applicant has been convicted of, or is under pending indictment for enumerated disqualifiers, as set forth within this chapter.
v. A person who has consented to the City for a criminal history based on fingerprinting record may request and receive a copy of the criminal history record report from the City at no additional charge. Should the person seek to amend or correct the record, he or she shall be responsible for contacting the GCIC as to State records and/or the FBI concerning records from other jurisdictions maintained in its file.
(9) Failure to furnish required information, and in the form designated, shall automatically serve to dismiss the application; and
(10) All applications shall be signed and sworn to by the applicant before a notary public or other officer authorized to administer oaths.
(11) In addition to the application fee due to the Police Department, the applicant shall also pay a $50.00 application fee to the Planning and Inspections Department to process the application.
(12) The City shall have 14 calendar days after the application is completed and filed with the City Manager or his/her designee in which to investigate the applicant and issue or deny the license. No license to operate a Hookah Bar or Lounge will be issued if the applicant:
a. Has been convicted of, or has entered a plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude, illegal gambling, any felony, criminal trespass, public indecency, misdemeanor involving any type of sexual-related crime, any theft or violence against person or property, any crime of possession, sale, or distribution of illegal drugs, distribution of material depicting nudity or sexual conduct as defined under state law, criminal solicitation to commit any of these listed offenses, attempts to commit any of these listed offenses, for a period of five years prior to the date of application for such certificate and has been released from parole or probation. As used herein, the term "a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude" shall include any misdemeanor criminal offenses involving fraud, theft, dishonesty and misdemeanor drug offenses. However, all applicants shall be entitled to the full benefits of O.C.G.A. § 42-8-60 et seq. relating to first offender status. If, at the time of application, the applicant is charged with any of the offenses prescribed in this subsection, then consideration of the application shall be suspended until the entry of a plea or verdict or dismissal;
b. Has had any previous license to operate a hookah bar or lounge revoked; or
c. Has violated any other hookah bar or lounge regulation.
(13) In any case in which it appears to the City Manager or his/her designee that an applicant is not entitled to the issuance of a license under the provisions of this chapter, the City Manager or his/her designee shall so notify the applicant in writing by mailing said notice to the last address furnished by the applicant. In the event that the City Manager or his/her designee refuses to issue a hookah bar or lounge license, or in the event that a hookah bar or lounge license is surrendered pursuant to the provisions of this chapter, the applicant or license holder shall have an absolute right of appeal to the City Manager according to the procedures set forth herein. The appeal shall be perfected by filing with the City Manager a notice of appeal. The notice of appeal must be filed with the City Manager within 14 days following the mailing of the notification of denial or surrender of the license. Thereafter, the City Manager shall set a date for hearing on the matter within 30 days after the City Manager's receipt of the notice of appeal. Moreover, the City Manager shall notify the appellant in writing of the date, time and place when the matter shall be heard. After the hearing, the City Manager shall inform the applicant of their decision within 14 calendar days of the hearing, and the City Manager's decision shall be final.
(Ord. No. 1323, § 1, 5-17-2023)
1328:
In addition to general revocation conditions, the license of any hookah bar or lounge operator may be revoked for:
(1) Being convicted of, or entering a plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, any felony or to any misdemeanor involving moral turpitude, as such term is defined within this chapter. (c) In the event that the annual license fee is not timely paid, then a penalty of ten percent of the license fee shall be assessed as a late penalty.
(Ord. No. 1323, § 1, 5-17-2023)
1331:
Sworn officers of the police department shall have the authority to inspect establishments registered under this chapter during hours in which the premises are open for business. (Ord. No. 1323, § 1, 5-17-2023)
1332:
Any person who shall conduct a business or occupation without having first obtained a hookah bar or lounge license, or who shall violate any other provision of this chapter, shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished as provided in Article II, Section 2 of the Charter. 1334:
A. The purpose of this chapter is to ensure the continued availability of quality transient lodging within the City, proper maintenance of hotels and to protect the health, safety and welfare of hotel inhabitants.
B. Unless otherwise stated in this chapter, the requirements of this chapter apply to those who occupy, visit, patronize, frequent, operate, keep, conduct, or own a hotel within the City, regardless of the date of the hotel's construction.
C. This chapter is essential to the public's interest, safety, health and welfare, and this chapter shall be liberally construed to effectuate its purposes.
(Ord. No. 1375, § 1, 6-26-2024)
1335:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Bona fide employee shall mean a person who works in the service of the hotel (i.e. the employer) under a contract of hire, whether express or implied, where the employer has the power or right to control or direct the details of what work is to be performed and the manner in which that work is to be performed.
Good repair shall refer to the condition of a hotel room in which all essential amenities and facilities are functional, and there are no significant defects or hazards that may compromise the health, safety or welfare of its occupants. A hotel room in good repair means that it is well-maintained, clean, free of pests, and free from any visible damages or defects. It shall have functioning amenities, such as lights, plumbing, heating/cooling systems, electric outlets and electronic devices. Additionally, the furniture, fixtures, furnishing and decor should be in good condition without signs of wear and tear.
Guest shall mean a person who is not a patron who is present on the premises of a hotel with the express permission of (a) another guest or a patron of the hotel, and (b) the owner, operator, keeper or proprietor of the hotel.
Hotel or motel shall, for the purpose of this chapter, mean any structure consisting of one or more buildings, with more than five dwelling units with provisions for transient living, sanitation, and sleeping, that is specifically constructed, kept, used, maintained, advertised, and held out to the public to be a place where temporary lodging is offered for pay to guests. For the purposes of this chapter, a hotel shall also include any structure that could be described as a roominghouse/boardinghouse, as that term is defined in Section 8-7-15 of this Code.
Housekeeping shall mean the cleaning of guest rooms, guest bathrooms, public area, changing of linen and removal of trash from guest rooms and common areas.
Loitering. A person commits the offense of loitering when the person is in a place at a time or in a manner not usual for law-abiding individuals under circumstances that warrant a justifiable and reasonable alarm or immediate concern for the safety of persons or property in the vicinity.
Patron shall mean a person who pays a fee to the owner, operator, keeper or proprietor of the hotel.
Police chief shall mean the City of Conyers' Chief of Police or his/her designee.
Public nuisance shall mean a condition, obstruction or use of property allowed or continued by any person, legal entity or agent, that interferes with the comfortable enjoyment of life and property by the neighborhood, community, or members of the public; or which can cause hurt, damage, inconvenience or affect or offend an ordinary, reasonable person.
Vehicle is any car, truck, trailer, motorcycle, or other machinery used for transporting people or goods and is normally required to be registered with a state in order to be legally operated or towed on a public roadway.
Visitor shall mean a person, who is not a patron or guest, who is on the premises of a hotel at the invitation of a patron or guest, but without the express permission of the owner, operator, keeper or proprietor of the hotel.
(Ord. No. 1375, § 1, 6-26-2024)
1336:
A. An owner, operator, keeper or proprietor of a hotel may designate no more than five percent or six rooms, whichever is fewer, for the purpose of allowing any number of bona fide employees and their family to reside on the premises. (Ord. No. 1375, § 1, 6-26-2024)
1337:
A. No hotel located within the City shall allow any person to occupy such hotel for more than 180 consecutive days without first meeting the requirements set forth in this section.
B. On or before the 180th consecutive day that a guest has occupied a hotel room, the owner, operator, keeper or proprietor of the hotel must conduct a thorough and documented inspection of the hotel room to ensure that it complies with the standards of good repair, as defined hereinabove. A new inspection must occur on or before each 180-day period that a guest occupies a hotel room.
C. If a hotel room is found to need repairs or maintenance to comply with the definition of good repair, then the owner, operator, keeper or proprietor of the hotel shall promptly address said repairs or maintenance and shall conduct such repairs or maintenance that are necessary to bring said hotel room into compliance with the standard of good repair.
D. A stay in a hotel room in excess of 180 consecutive days without a documented inspection and a finding of good repair may occur in the following situations:
1. Where there is a written contract or documented agreement between a hotel and a business, corporation, firm or governmental agency to house employees or individuals on valid work orders;
2. Where there is documentation, consistent with HIPPA privacy rules, that a hotel guest is considered family or is providing care for a patient who is admitted at local hospital; or
3. When an insurance company or federal, state or local agency has provided documentation that a hotel guest has been displaced from their home by a catastrophic disaster or fire.
(Ord. No. 1375, § 1, 6-26-2024)
1339:
A. No applicant shall operate, conduct, manage, engage in, or carry on a hotel under any name other than his/her name and the name of the business as specified on the occupation tax certificate.
B. Any application for an extension or expansion of a building or other place of business where a hotel is located shall require inspection, and all extension or expansion shall comply with all applicable codes and regulations.
(Ord. No. 1375, § 1, 6-26-2024)
1340:
A. It shall be unlawful for any person to rent or occupy any room in any hotel for any illegal or unlawful purposes, or for the owner, operator, keeper or proprietor of any such hotel to rent, assign to or permit any patron or guest to occupy any such room, with knowledge that they intend to use it for illegal or unlawful purposes.
B. It shall also be unlawful to rent or occupy any room in any hotel for otherwise legal commercial activity from any guest rooms or common areas without first obtaining approval from the City.
C. It shall be unlawful for any patron, guest or other individual to advertise on any website, social media, printed material, radio or television advertisement any business, service or product (whether lawful or unlawful) being delivered, offered, performed, created, distributed, or otherwise transacted from any room within a hotel.
(Ord. No. 1375, § 1, 6-26-2024)
1341:
A. All patrons and guests who wish to park a vehicle on hotel premises must register said vehicle with the hotel operator upon initial registration, during any future re-registration, or at any time after registration when they begin parking a vehicle on hotel premises. Hotel operators must record the vehicle's identifying information, which shall include, but not be limited to, the make and model of the vehicle, the tag number of the vehicle, and the state of issuance of the tag.
B. All handicapped parking must comply with state and local laws.
C. All vehicles parked on any hotel's premises must be in good working order, including but not limited to, compliance with the City's junk vehicle ordinance, which is found in Section 8-7-93(o) of this Code.
D. Vehicle maintenance in hotel parking lots is prohibited.
E. Every operator, owner, keeper, or proprietor of any hotel shall remove any vehicle from the hotel's premises within 48 hours of being notified that said vehicle is in violation of this subsection.
(Ord. No. 1375, § 1, 6-26-2024)
1342:
Every operator, owner, keeper, or proprietor of any hotel shall comply with the following requirements:
A. Every operator, owner, keeper, or proprietor of any hotel shall keep and maintain in each and every rental unit, a telephone equipped to place a direct call to 911. It shall not be deemed sufficient compliance with this requirement if a person must first dial "9" on the telephone before dialing 9-1-1, nor shall it deemed to be sufficient compliance if a call must first go through the front desk of the hotel before dialing 911.
B. No operator, owner, keeper, or proprietor of any hotel shall rent or provide a room for any number of persons greater than the sleeping accommodations provided within the particular rental unit or temporary sleeping accommodations provided by the hotel.
C. No operator, owner, keeper, or proprietor, patron, visitor or guest of any hotel shall be allowed to congregate within any room or single rental unit a number of persons that is greater than two times the number of persons for whom sleeping accommodations are provided within the single room or rental unit, except when temporarily designated as a hospitality suite by the hotel.
D. Daily housekeeping shall be included within the standard room rate of any hotel. At a minimum, rooms must be cleaned before each new guest checks in and no less frequently than twice every seven days. Each hotel must maintain a log that documents when each room is cleaned. The log must be maintained for 180 days.
E. All guestroom linens shall be in good condition, clean and free of stains. Torn, damaged, stained or worn linen are prohibited. Hotels shall maintain, on site, a minimum supply of linen sufficient to accommodate a daily 100 percent occupancy room turnover. All occupied guestrooms shall be supplied with a minimum of two bath towels, two hand towels and two washcloths. Guests in rooms with more than two guests at one time shall be allotted an additional towel, hand towel and wash cloth for each additional guest.
F. The utilization of clothes-lines or other clothes-drying equipment or facilities outside of a room that are located on or are visible from the outside of a room are prohibited. Balconies and railings are not to be used for hanging, linens, towels, personal items or any other articles of clothing.
G. Each guestroom in any hotel shall be numbered in a plain, conspicuous manner. Such numbers shall be at least three inches high and shall be placed at approximately five feet from the ground on the outside of the outer door of each guestroom. No two guestrooms shall bear the same number.
H. All exterior lights shall be maintained in good working order, and all lighting fixtures shall remain in good repair. Exterior lighting fixtures shall comply with the requirements in Section 8-7-86.1 of this Code.
I. All guestrooms shall have an evacuation route posted on the interior side of the exit door.
J. All guestrooms shall be equipped with a hard-wired, operational smoke detector that is approved by the Fire Marshal.
(Ord. No. 1375, § 1, 6-26-2024; Ord. No. 1462, § 1, 11-19-2025)
1343:
A. The open parking area and all areas surrounding any building or proposed building being a hotel shall have an average maintained footcandle intensity of at least one footcandle with a minimum allowable intensity of three-tenths of a footcandle. The covered parking area of any hotel shall have an average maintained footcandle intensity of five-tenths of a footcandle. All lighting must also comply with Section 8-7-86.1 of this Code for exterior lighting requirements.
B. Parking lots shall remain in a reasonable state of repair and must be resurfaced in cases of excessive patching of potholes and widespread fracturing of asphalt.
C. Grilling is only allowed in designated areas and where all applicable safety codes and regulations are met. Grilling is not permitted in guestrooms or on guestroom balconies.
D. Graffiti and markings or insignia that may indicate the presence or association of a street gang shall be removed in a timeline compliant with the graffiti ordinance set forth in Chapter 4 of Title 11 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 1375, § 1, 6-26-2024)
1344:
A. Definitions.
Existing hotel means a hotel that held a valid City business license and was operating within the City as of December 1, 2025.
New hotel means any hotel that is first opened for guest occupancy within the City after December 1, 2025.
Smoking means inhaling, exhaling, burning, or carrying any lighted bidi, cigar, cigarette, pipe, weed, plant, or other combustible substance in any manner or in any form, including vaping and the use of electronic smoking devices.
Smoke-free means that smoking is prohibited in 100 percent of a hotel's guestrooms.
Smoking room means a guestroom in which smoking is allowed.
B. Smoking is prohibited in all indoor areas and common areas of all hotels, except in guestrooms designated as a smoking room for existing hotels, as set forth in this section. Smoking is also expressly prohibited in exterior breezeways, sidewalks, stairwells, or within 15 feet of any guest room or doors used for ingress or egress.
C. Each hotel shall provide no more than one designated outdoor smoking area. The outdoor smoking area shall not be located within the parking lot of the hotel to prevent guests, patrons, employees, or visitors from loitering in the parking lot to smoke. The designated smoking area shall be no closer to any door used for ingress or egress than that specified in item B.
D. An existing hotel may designate smoking rooms in an amount not to exceed 20 percent of its total guest rooms, rounded down to the nearest whole room. Each designated smoking room shall be clearly identified in the existing hotel's internal room inventory. The existing hotel shall maintain a current floor plan identifying designated smoking rooms, and the existing hotel shall provide the current floor plan to the City upon request.
E. If an existing hotel is smoke-free as of December 1, 2025, or if it later becomes smoke-free, then it shall remain smoke-free thereafter. If any existing hotel later undergoes a change in ownership, then that existing hotel shall immediately become smoke-free.
F. New hotels shall be smoke-free.
G. Certification. Each hotel shall, by January 31 of each year, file with the City's Planning and Inspection Services Department a certification on a City-provided form stating (i) if the hotel is smoke-free; or (ii) if an existing hotel with designated smoking rooms: the total number of guest rooms, the number of guest rooms designated as smoking rooms, and the location of each smoking room.
H. Signage. For every designated non-smoking room, there shall be clearly and conspicuously posted at the entrance of said room a "No Smoking" sign that is not less than three inches in diameter with letters not less than one inch in height or a sign with the international no smoking symbol (consisting of a pictorial representation of a burning cigarette enclosed in a red circle with a red bar across it). For every designated smoking room, there shall be clearly and conspicuously posted at the entrance of said room a sign indicating that smoking is permitted.
(Ord. No. 1375, § 1, 6-26-2024; Ord. No. 1462, § 2, 11-19-2025)
1345:
A. For the purpose of this chapter, "video surveillance system" (hereinafter "VSS") means a continuous digital surveillance system including cameras, cabling, monitors, and digital video recorders (DVR).
B. Every owner, operator, keeper or proprietor of any new or existing hotel is required to install a VSS within 180 days of March 1, 2024. All hotels that have installed a VSS prior to the effective date of this chapter shall ensure said VSS is in full compliance with this chapter and shall request an approval assessment from the Police Chief within 180 days of the effective date of this chapter.
C. All VSS shall be maintained in proper working order at all times, be kept in continuous operation 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and meet the minimum technological standards established in this chapter. The hotel shall retain the continuous digital recordings by this system for no less than 30 days.
D. All VSS shall have no less than one camera dedicated to each register or check-out stand, entrance/exit, interior hallway and lobby, swimming pool area, exercise facility, loading dock, and all parking areas. The placement of cameras included in VSS required under this chapter must be approved by the Police Chief or his/her designee. Existing VSS at any hotel as of the effective date of this chapter will be evaluated to ensure full compliance with this chapter.
E. The VSS shall be subject to regular inspection by the Police Chief, or his/her designee, who is authorized to inspect any such system at reasonable times to determine whether it conforms to this chapter. If the VSS does not conform, the hotel, in question, shall take immediate steps, not to exceed 30 days, to bring the system back into compliance.
F. The Police Chief or his/her designee may develop, maintain and publish on the City website additional VSS standards for VSS equipment, installation, and maintenance. Any new standards or changes to existing standards may be issued in conjunction with annual business license renewal notices and become effective on January 1 of each year.
(Ord. No. 1375, § 1, 6-26-2024)

A. All hotel operators will advise patrons and guests verbally, upon registration, and through posted signage that loitering is prohibited.

(a) Whenever any Police Officer finds a vehicle standing upon a street or highway in violation of any of the foregoing provisions of this chapter, the officer is hereby authorized to move the vehicle or require the driver or other person in charge of the vehicle to move the same, to a position off the paved or main-traveled part of such street or highway.

A. When not inconsistent with this chapter or any ordinance, the City Manager and Chief of Police are authorized to prohibit parking or stopping of vehicles on any street or portion of a street when traffic and engineering surveys indicate that such stopping or parking may impede the free flow of traffic on such street, including, but not limited to the following:

b. When official signs prohibiting parking are erected upon narrow streets as authorized herein, no person shall park a vehicle upon the street in violation of the sign.

1377:
The following application procedures shall govern special event permits:
a. Applications for special event permits shall be submitted on a form provided by the City Manager or his/her designee. A nonrefundable application fee shall accompany the application as established by the City Council, from time to time, to defray the cost of processing the application. The complete application must be submitted at least 60 days prior to the starting day of the proposed special event.
b. The application shall contain each of the following unless the City Manager or his/her designee deems an item inapplicable to the type of event proposed:
i. Name, address, phone and email of the applicant.
ii. Delineation of boundaries. The outermost boundaries of the special event shall be fully and clearly delineated on a map, which shall be no smaller than 8½ by 11 inches in size, and attached to the application for a permit. All public streets and/or sidewalks within and adjacent to such area(s) shall be clearly identified. The city manager or his/her designee shall require, as part of the approval for the special event, that areas no less than five feet in width shall be designated and preserved for public circulation and access to adjoining business establishments outside the area(s) delineated for the special event.
iii. The date(s), hours and duration of the special event.
iv. Estimated attendance figures.
v. Completed and signed application forms.
vi. A statement of the type of special event proposed.
vii. If the special event is to be located on public property, obtain and maintain for the duration of the special event comprehensive general liability insurance in a minimum amount of $1,000,000.00 combined limits for bodily injury and/or property damage that names the City as an additional named insured. A certificate evidencing such insurance shall be provided with the application.
c. If the special event permit application is approved, then a non-refundable permit fee shall be paid by the applicant prior to the issuance of the special event permit. The permit fee shall be established by the City Council.
(Code 1978, § 9-2003; Code 1990, § 10-2-3; Ord. No. 530, 4-19-1993; Ord. No. 825, § 1(10-2-3), 5-4-2011; Ord. No. 1280, § 1, 3-16-2022)

1379:

(a) After considering all comments and conditions of the reviewing Departments as well as other information pertaining to the proposed event as described on the application, and after the payment of all applicable fees and costs, the City Manager or his/her designee shall approve or conditionally approve the application and issue a special event permit for a special event upon a finding that satisfactory provisions and arrangements have been made by the applicant concerning all requirements of this chapter to the satisfaction of each reviewing Department. 1392:
This chapter is adopted to address the interest of public safety. Motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles, low-speed vehicles and other similar vehicles are not designed or manufactured to be used on public highways, streets and roads, (hereafter "public streets"), and the City in no way advocates their operation on the public streets within its jurisdiction. Adoption of this chapter is not to be relied upon as a determination by the City that the operation of motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles, low-speed vehicles and other similar vehicles on public streets is safe or advisable if done in accordance with this chapter. By regulating such operation, the City is merely addressing safety issues. All persons who operate or ride in motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles, low-speed vehicles and other similar vehicles on public streets do so with their own judgment and at their own risk, and must be observant of, and attentive to the safety of themselves and others, including their passengers, other motorists, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, the City of Conyers has no liability in negligence, nuisance or under any other cause of action for losses resulting from the use of motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles, low-speed vehicles, and other similar vehicles on streets, roads, sidewalks, rights-of-way or other public property under this chapter. Any person who operates motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles, low-speed vehicles and other similar vehicles is responsible for procuring appropriate insurance as may be required by any State of Georgia law or this chapter as a condition of operating motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles, low-speed vehicles and other similar vehicles on the public streets in the City of Conyers.
(Ord. No. 962, § 1, 6-4-2014)
1393:
The following words and phrases when used in this chapter shall have the definitions respectively ascribed to them in this chapter.
All-terrain vehicle means any motorized vehicle designed for off-road use which is equipped with three or more low pressure tires and with a seat to be straddled by the operator and with handlebars for steering control. All-terrain vehicles are prohibited to be operated on public streets by this chapter.
Electric personal assistive mobility device (EPAMD) means a self-balancing, two nontandem wheeled device designed to transport only one person and having an electric propulsion system with average power of 750 watts (one horsepower) and a maximum speed of less than 20 miles per hour on a paved level surface when powered solely by such propulsion system.
Gross weight means the unladen weight of the vehicle plus the weight of any load thereon.
Low-speed vehicle (LSV) means any four-wheeled electric vehicle whose top speed attainable in one mile is greater than 20 miles per hour but not greater than 25 miles per hour on a paved level surface and which is manufactured in compliance with those federal motor vehicle safety standards for low-speed vehicles set forth in 49 C.F.R. Section 571.500 and in effect on January 1, 2001.
Motorized cart (MC) means every motor vehicle having no less than three wheels and an unladen weight of l,300 pounds or less and which cannot operate at more than 20 miles per hour.
Motor vehicle means every vehicle which is self-propelled other than an electric personal assistive mobility device (EPAMD).
Pedestrian means any person afoot.
Personal transportation vehicle (PTV) means any motor vehicle with a minimum of four wheels, capable of a maximum level ground speed of less than 20 miles per hour with a maximum gross vehicle unladen or empty weight of 1,375 pounds and capable of transporting not more than eight persons. The term does not include mobility aids, including power wheelchairs and scooters, which can be used indoors and outdoors for the express purpose of enabling mobility for a person with a disability. The term also does not include any all-terrain vehicle.
Public street means the entire width between the boundary lines of every right-of-way or place open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular travel within the boundaries of the City of Conyers, including alleys.
Sidewalk means that portion of public property of a street between the curb lines, or the lateral lines of a railway, and the adjacent property lines, intended for use only by pedestrians.
Unladen weight means the weight of a vehicle without load as per the manufacturer's specifications for such vehicle.
Valid motor vehicle driver's license means any current and valid certificate issued by the State of Georgia, any other state of the United States of America, or international agency which permits persons to operate motor vehicles on the public roads of the State of Georgia.
Vehicle means every device in, upon, or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, excepting devices used exclusively upon stationary rails or tracks.
(Ord. No. 962, § 1, 6-4-2014)

Any personal transportation vehicle, as defined by this chapter, which also qualifies as a motorized cart, as defined by this chapter, shall only be considered a motorized cart under this chapter and be subject only to the requirements, including registration, equipment, and inspections for motorized carts under this chapter.
(Ord. No. 962, § 1, 6-4-2014)
1395:
(a) Any owner desiring to allow a motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle to be operated on City streets must first register the motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle with the City of Conyers on an application form provided by the City. A fee of $15.00 shall be required to register a motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle. The registration of such vehicle shall be for the purposes of permitting that owner to allow such motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle to be operated on the public streets by qualified operators during the applicable registration year. In the event that the ownership of any motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle is transferred to another owner during the registration year, that new owner must seek and obtain a new registration from the City prior to the new owner's operation of their motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle on public streets within the City.
(b) The registration year for all motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles or low speed vehicles shall run from July 1 through June 30. The registration of the motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle shall allow such vehicle to be operated on the public streets of the City from the date of registration through June 30 of the current registration year. Each motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle must have a current registration in order to be operated on the public streets of the City.
(c) It shall be the duty of every operator of a motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle, and low speed vehicle that is operated on public streets in the City of Conyers to ensure that the motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle, and low speed vehicle has a current registration with the City of Conyers prior to operating such vehicle on public streets within the City of Conyers.
(d) All applications to register a motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle with the City of Conyers shall include the model, make, vehicle identification number or serial number of the motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle which is being registered. All applications shall also include the name and address of the owner, a contact phone number, and any other such information as the City shall deem appropriate at the time of such application.
(e) Upon the successful registration of a motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle with the City of Conyers, the City of Conyers shall issue the owner a registration decal signifying such registration. The decal must be affixed to the rear of the motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle in such a manner as to be visible at all times. The registration decal shall remain permanently affixed to the motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle during that registration year unless the motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle is destroyed.
(f) No registration decal may be transferred from one motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle to another motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle. The registration decal is specific to only the motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle which was registered at the time of the issuance of the registration decal.
(g) No registration decal may be transferred from one owner of a motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle to a successive owner of such motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle. The registration decal is specific to only the owner that applied for such registration decal and may not be transferred to a subsequent owner.
(h) The failure to have a current registration license decal affixed to a motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle being operated on the public streets within the City of Conyers shall be a violation of this chapter and shall subject the operator of such motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle to the penalties set forth in the City of Conyers Code of Ordinances.
(i) Only those persons 18 years of age and older with a valid driver's license may seek to register a motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle. The registration issued by the City of Conyers must be in the owner's name only and the registration form must be signed by that person.
(j) The City Manager may, at his/her discretion waive registration requirements for special events of a limited duration to which non-residents of the City of Conyers may operate unregistered motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles or low speed vehicles on designated public streets within the City. Such special events shall last no longer than seven calendar days.
(Ord. No. 962, § 1, 6-4-2014)
1396:

Head lights and tail lamps must be activated and operational at all times such motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle is in use.
(b) Any low-speed vehicle being operated on the public streets within the City shall display an amber strobe light which shall be visible under normal atmospheric conditions from a distance of 500 feet from the front and rear of such vehicle.

1397:
(a) All gasoline-powered motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles or low speed vehicles shall at all times be equipped with an exhaust system in good working order and in constant operation, meeting the following specifications:
(1) The exhaust system shall include the piping leading from the flange of the exhaust manifold to and including the muffler and exhaust pipes or include any and all parts specified by the manufacturer.
(2) The exhaust system in its own shall be securely fastened, including the consideration of missing or broken brackets or hangers.
(3) The engine and power mechanism of every gasoline-powered motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle shall be so equipped, adjusted, and tuned, as to prevent the escape of excessive smoke or fumes.
(b) It shall be unlawful for the owner of any gasoline-powered motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle to operate or permit the operation of such gasoline-powered motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle on the public streets within the City of Conyers on which any device controlling or abating atmospheric conditions which is placed on the gasoline-powered motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle by the manufacturer has been removed, is non-operational, or is not operating as designed.
(c) All gasoline-powered motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles and low speed vehicles shall be maintained in good working order and kept in good condition and shall be subject to inspection by City officials at reasonable times and intervals.
(d) All gasoline-powered motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles and low speed vehicles shall be maintained in such condition so that they are incapable of "backfiring," or otherwise operating so as to make loud noises.
(Ord. No. 962, § 1, 6-4-2014)
1398:

1399:
(a) Motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles and low speed vehicles may only be operated on designated public streets within the City. In no event shall the speed limit on public streets designated to permit the operation thereon of motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles or low speed vehicles be greater than 35 miles per hour.
(1) The public streets within the City upon which the operation of motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles and low speed vehicles shall be permitted shall only include those public streets specified on the City of Conyers Motorized Cart Map, which is set forth in Exhibit A, which is attached to the ordinance codified in this section and incorporated by reference as if fully set forth herein. The City of Conyers Motorized Cart Map will be kept on file and available for public inspection during regular business hours at the Conyers Police Department and at the customer service desk at Conyers City Hall. A copy of the City of Conyers Motorized Cart Map shall be provided to all owners who are issued a registration decal for a motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle.
(b) Motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles and low speed vehicles shall not be operated on sidewalks, multi-purpose paths (Olde Town Conyers Trail), in parks, playgrounds, greenspace, City right-of-way (aside from approved public streets), or front yards.

(f) The maximum occupancy of motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles and low speed vehicles being operated on the public streets within the City shall not exceed one person per seat as designed by the manufacturer or such vehicle.
(g) All operators of motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles and low speed vehicles shall abide by all traffic regulations applicable to motorized vehicular traffic when operating a motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle on the public streets within the City.
(h) No all-terrain vehicle shall be permitted to operate on any public roads, sidewalks, rights-of-way or other public property of the City. Violations will be prosecuted under the O.C.G.A., tit. 40, ch. 7, pertaining to "off-road vehicles."
(i) Motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles and low speed vehicles shall not be used in the operation of a taxicab service or any type vehicle for hire operation.

1400:
(a) The operation of motorized cart, personal transportation vehicle or low speed vehicle on the public streets within the City of Conyers shall comply in every respect with the requirements of Georgia law, including, without limitation, the provisions of the O.C.G.A. §§ 40-6-330 and 40-6-331, and all other statutory regulations applicable to vehicular traffic and safety equipment.
(b) Only those persons possessing a valid motor vehicle driver's license issued by the State of Georgia, another state of the United States of America, or international agency which permits such person to operate a motor vehicle on the highways of the State may operate and drive motorized carts, personal transportation and low speed vehicles on the designated public streets within the City of Conyers.
